sections.title: Separate the route from the conversation.

Check availability before selecting a human destination.

Check the route does not return to its starting point.

Update rules when operating availability changes.

title: Call transfer script and handoff language
description: Review call transfer language for your service business: understand the workflow, check the supported setup and give your team a clear next step.
lead: Explain the handoff before moving the call.
intro: Call transfer language should tell the caller what will happen and give the recipient useful context. Match the wording to the actual transfer method and the receiving person’s availability.

sections.title: Explain the next step and ask about holding.
paragraphs: Before a transfer, state the reason for involving another person. Useful wording is “I can try to connect you with the team for that question. Are you able to hold?” Use it only when trying that connection is supported by the business’s rules.

A transfer attempt is different from a promise that someone will answer. Avoid telling the caller a technician is ready, a request is urgent enough for dispatch or a quote will be available unless the responsible person has confirmed that commitment.
items: State the reason for the handoff.
Ask whether the caller can hold.
Describe a connection attempt accurately.

sections.title: Brief the recipient when the method supports it.
paragraphs: For an attended transfer, provide the request and essential context before connecting the caller. A concise structure is the reason for the call, verified contact details and the decision the caller needs. Do not add guessed facts to make the briefing sound complete.

A blind transfer may not support a spoken pre-brief. Confirm the available handoff information and avoid saying that the recipient has already been briefed when that is not true. Keep the recipient’s accepted role separate from the general intake script.
items: Share the request and verified details.
Explain what decision needs a person.
Match the wording to the actual transfer method.

sections.title: Give an unavailable-recipient response.
paragraphs: If the connection is not completed, explain the supported next step. “The team is unavailable to take the call now. What is the best number for a callback?” is appropriate when a callback request is the actual fallback. State response timing only if the business has authorized it.

Revo lists transfers on higher tiers. Confirm the supported method, recipient behavior and unavailable fallback directly. Test the wording with authorized participants, including the case where the receiving person cannot answer.
items: Use the actual no-answer fallback.
Confirm a callback number if collecting a request.
Test recipient availability and the resulting caller message.

faqs.q: Should I say the recipient has all the details?
faqs.a: Only when that briefing or information delivery has actually occurred through the supported process.

faqs.q: Can these phrases be used for every transfer?
faqs.a: Adapt them to the approved business rules, supported transfer method and real fallback. Do not make availability promises the team has not authorized.

title: Turn off call forwarding and restore incoming calls
description: Review turn off forwarding for your service business: understand the workflow, check the supported setup and give your team a clear next step.
lead: Verify the original route after disabling forwarding.
intro: Turning off call forwarding is a rollback task. If calls still fail to reach the original phone, distinguish a forwarding setting from other restrictions before changing additional settings.

sections.title: Identify the route you need to undo.
paragraphs: Record the provider, line type and forwarding condition that was enabled. Immediate forwarding, conditional forwarding and phone-system routing can have separate controls. Use the current instructions for that service; a code for another carrier is not a reliable reset.

For supported Verizon wireless forwarding, the official deactivation instructions specify *73 and the provider’s confirmation steps. The separate Verizon and T-Mobile setup guides cover their documented controls. For a hosted business system or fixed line, use its administrator or provider instructions.
items: Identify the provider, service class and changed condition.
Use the matching official deactivation method.
Keep unrelated routes and account settings unchanged.

sections.title: Test ringing and voicemail after the change.
paragraphs: Use an authorized call from another number to check that the original phone receives the call. Then test the intended no-answer and voicemail behavior. A confirmation tone or saved setting does not substitute for checking what the caller actually reaches.

If the call still reaches an answering destination, record the observed behavior and ask the provider to check the active route. Avoid guessing additional codes or routing a destination back to the starting number. Keep the business’s temporary callback process clear while the provider resolves the configuration.
items: Test an ordinary incoming call.
Check no-answer and voicemail behavior.
Record the unexpected destination for provider support.

sections.title: Check restrictions when forwarding is already off.
paragraphs: Verizon’s official guidance tells users who still cannot receive calls to check restrictions such as Do Not Disturb, blocking and apps that limit incoming calls. Review the relevant settings for the device and service without assuming a forwarding reset resolves them.

If the problem persists, contact the provider with the test result, affected line and time of the test. Do not publish customer call details or transfer credentials. Once the original route works, review any later Revo routing change as a separate authorized configuration and test it again.
items: Check applicable device and service restrictions.
Give the provider the relevant test observations.
Verify the original route before reactivating answering coverage.

faqs.q: Is there a universal code to turn forwarding off?
faqs.a: No. Use the official method for the provider, line type and condition. Verizon’s documented wireless *73 method must not be generalized to every carrier.

faqs.q: Why might calls still fail after forwarding is off?
faqs.a: Other device, account or app restrictions may affect incoming calls. Check applicable settings and contact the provider with the observed test results.

takeaway: Verify the original route after disabling forwarding.

title: Automated appointment reminders vs booking confirmation
description: Review appointment reminders for your service business: understand the workflow, check the supported setup and give your team a clear next step.
lead: Keep reminders aligned with the actual appointment.
intro: An automated appointment reminder is a scheduled outbound communication about an existing appointment. It is different from collecting a time request or confirming a booking during an incoming call.

sections.title: Use the confirmed appointment as the source.
paragraphs: A reminder should refer to an appointment that actually exists in the business’s scheduling system. Confirm the customer contact, time zone and visit details before scheduling a message. An unaccepted request for a time is not enough to tell a customer a visit is booked.

Keep the system of record and its owner clear. When an appointment changes or is canceled, the pending reminder must follow that change through the supported workflow. Otherwise a message can describe an obsolete visit even though it was scheduled correctly at first.
items: Use the confirmed appointment record.
Check contact details and the time zone.
Identify who maintains appointment changes.

sections.title: Review delivery, cancellation and replies.
paragraphs: A scheduled message and a delivered message are different states. Twilio’s official messaging documentation, for example, describes scheduling and cancellation as distinct controls and documents send-time failures. Confirm the corresponding behavior of the actual system your business uses.

Decide who handles replies requesting a new time or reporting a problem. Check the provider’s messaging and opt-out requirements before use. Review the content for unnecessary personal details and use authorized tests; do not assume that a reminder proves the customer read it or will attend.
items: Verify scheduling and delivery status separately.
Test changed or canceled appointments.
Assign reply handling and review opt-out behavior.

sections.title: Separate this workflow from Revo’s published offer.
paragraphs: Revo’s website lists appointment booking and SMS follow-up. Those labels do not verify a native scheduled outbound appointment-reminder service. Confirm that specific capability and any supported scheduling connection directly before attributing it to Revo.

Review the incoming booking workflow with Revo and the later reminder workflow with the scheduling or messaging provider. Keep one owner responsible for ensuring the confirmed appointment reaches the supported downstream process. This guide does not claim a particular integration, reminder timing or reduction in missed appointments.
items: Confirm Revo’s supported booking outcome.
Verify the reminder capability with the actual provider.
Assign responsibility for the handoff between workflows.

faqs.q: Is SMS follow-up proof of automated reminders?
faqs.a: No. A follow-up feature does not by itself establish scheduled reminders tied to future appointments. Confirm the exact capability.

faqs.q: Does Revo send scheduled appointment reminders?
faqs.a: This page does not establish that capability. Ask Revo about the current supported setup, and keep reminder scheduling separate from incoming appointment booking.

takeaway: Keep reminders aligned with the actual appointment.

title: IVR system cost: compare the full operating scope
description: Review ivr system cost for your service business: understand the workflow, check the supported setup and give your team a clear next step.
lead: Compare the menu, maintenance and answering work.
intro: An IVR system guides callers through a phone menu using keypad selections or speech. Its cost depends on the service model, usage and work required to maintain the flow, not just a single advertised rate.

sections.title: Define what the menu must accomplish.
paragraphs: An IVR can collect a selection and direct the caller toward information or a destination. Start with the decisions your business needs: selecting a department, hearing approved information or reaching an available person. A routing menu is not automatically a complete service-request conversation.

Write down the fallback for an unrecognized selection, a caller who does not respond and an unavailable destination. Compare offers against those outcomes. Do not assume a provider’s base menu feature includes every speech, intake, booking or human-transfer function you want.
items: List the caller outcomes required.
Define invalid-input and no-response fallbacks.
Check which tasks need conversation rather than a menu.

sections.title: Identify both service charges and maintenance work.
paragraphs: Current provider rate sheets can separate calling usage, phone numbers and optional speech features. Twilio’s public US Voice pricing is one documented rate sheet with multiple charge categories. A hosted bundle can use a different model; compare the actual agreement without importing another provider’s rates.

Add the business’s setup and maintenance responsibilities to the review: recording or editing prompts, updating destinations, checking hours and testing changes. Use quotes and your own usage records. Do not present a universal IVR price or claim a savings figure without the corresponding scope and evidence.
items: Review current plan and usage charges.
Check optional features and destination requirements.
Assign prompt, rule and testing maintenance.

sections.title: Compare IVR scope with Revo’s answering offer.
paragraphs: Revo publishes an AI answering service with its own script and rules, booking and summaries. This guide does not describe Revo as an IVR vendor or attribute keypad menus or advanced routing to it. Confirm the supported features and plan directly.

Compare the work completed for the caller and your team. A menu that selects a destination and a conversation that captures a service request are different outcomes. Review the route, intake details and unavailable-person fallback, then compare current costs for the scope your business actually needs.
items: Confirm the actual Revo answering workflow.
Compare equivalent caller and team outcomes.
Use the current offer and documented operating requirements.

faqs.q: Is there one standard IVR system price?
faqs.a: No. Service models, usage and included features vary. Review current provider terms and the work needed to maintain the system.

faqs.q: Is Revo an IVR system?
faqs.a: This page compares scopes. It does not establish that Revo supplies an IVR phone menu; confirm its supported answering features directly.

takeaway: Compare the menu, maintenance and answering work.

title: AI receptionist alternatives for home service businesses
description: Compare Revo, Avoca, Goodcall, Sameday and Smith.ai using published booking, transfer, integration and billing details for home service businesses.
lead: Compare the documented workflow, not a ranking.
intro: AI receptionist alternatives differ in where they create bookings, who receives a handoff, which software they connect to and how usage is billed. Compare five providers below. Published by Revo; documentation reviewed October 15, 2026. This is a comparison of published offerings, not hands-on performance results. Confirm the selected plan and setup directly with each provider.

sections.title: Avoca: job records and CSR handoff
paragraphs: Avoca documents inbound answering and scheduling. Its ServiceTitan integration page describes creating job records with customer details, service information and call notes. That is a named field-service workflow, rather than evidence that every calendar or CRM uses the same integration.

Its inbound product describes a contextual handoff to a CSR. Separate offerings can include human coverage, so confirm exactly who receives a transferred call and which products are included in the quote. A universal billing unit was not verified in the official pages reviewed; request written pricing and implementation terms.
items: Booking destination: documented ServiceTitan job records.
Handoff: CSR workflow; confirm recipient and any vendor-staffed coverage.
Billing: confirm the unit, implementation charges and contract in the quote.
Confirm the exact integration operations for your account.

sections.title: Goodcall: calendar workflows and customer-based billing
paragraphs: Goodcall’s product documentation describes calendar booking, CRM updates, recordings and transcripts, with Google Calendar and HighLevel among its examples. It also describes transferring calls to the business. Check the supported calendar, recipient and fallback; a calendar connection does not prove a native connection to every field-service platform.

Its pricing defines a unique customer by phone number within the month, rather than using conversation minutes as the billing unit. Allowances and additional-customer terms vary by plan. Confirm the tool allowance and supported operations needed for your workflow instead of comparing that customer allowance directly with another provider’s minutes.
items: Booking destination: supported calendar or connected workflow; verify yours.
Handoff: transfer to the business; confirm the unavailable-recipient fallback.
Billing: distinct customer phone numbers within the month.
Confirm the selected plan’s tool limits and connection details.

sections.title: Revo: answering plans with tier-specific connections
paragraphs: Revo’s published plans include round-the-clock answering, appointment booking, your own script and rules, and a dashboard with call summaries. Crew and Fleet add transfers to your team, field-service software connections, recordings and transcripts. Those additional features are excluded from Solo; do not treat the higher-tier list as a description of every Revo plan.

The plans include monthly minute allowances. Confirm additional-minute terms and Launch Offer conditions directly. The published field-service connection label does not establish a native connection to a particular named platform or its exact booking actions. Likewise, a transfer feature does not establish a warm-transfer method or vendor-provided live receptionists.
items: Booking destination: confirm the supported calendar or software action.
Handoff: team transfers on Crew and Fleet; confirm the method and recipient.
Billing: monthly minute allowances; check current terms.
Solo excludes team transfers, field-service connections and recordings/transcripts.

sections.title: Sameday: field-service scheduling and escalation
paragraphs: Sameday positions its AI CSR around home-service calls, appointment booking and escalation to the business’s people. Its official integration pages document scheduling and customer-data workflows with ServiceTitan and Jobber. Ask the provider to identify the operations available for your specific software account and plan.

The current pricing page lists starting minute allowances. Use that pricing evidence rather than interpreting conflicting unmetered language in comparison articles as a universal plan promise. Confirm the current overage terms and any language or integration requirements. Escalation to your staff is a different arrangement from a receptionist supplied by the provider.
items: Booking destination: documented ServiceTitan and Jobber workflows; verify operations.
Handoff: escalation to the business’s people; confirm the destination.
Billing: pricing lists starting minute allowances.
Confirm overages, selected-plan connections and language availability.

sections.title: Smith.ai: AI answering and live-agent options
paragraphs: Smith.ai’s AI product documents appointment scheduling, lead qualification, recordings, summaries and context-preserving transfers. Its published scheduling examples include Calendly. Confirm the exact calendar or field-service workflow rather than applying a broad integration count to every package.

Its AI pricing uses call-based allowances or rates. The product also distinguishes live-agent involvement and hybrid arrangements from routing to your own team. Charges and conditions depend on the type of escalation and chosen arrangement. Request those terms explicitly; access to vendor-staffed reception and a transfer to your employee are not interchangeable features.
items: Booking destination: supported scheduling connection; confirm the required system.
Handoff: team transfers and vendor live-agent arrangements are distinct.
Billing: call-based AI plans; confirm human-involvement conditions.
Confirm the AI or hybrid package and supported integration operations.

sections.title: Three differences that change the shortlist
paragraphs: A calendar event, a captured time request and a job record in field-service software are different outputs. Ask each shortlisted provider to show the record it creates and which details reach the person responsible for the work. A software name on a product page is a starting point, not proof of every operation your team needs.

Compare who answers a handoff and how usage is measured separately. Your employee, a vendor receptionist and an unavailable recipient require different fallbacks. A minute, a call and a distinct-customer allowance are also different units; use your call records and the current written terms rather than treating their included quantities as equivalent.
items: Booking: identify the actual destination and confirmed outcome.
Handoff: identify the recipient, hours and no-answer path.
Billing: compare the written unit and scope using your own records.

sections.title: Ask for the same demonstration from each provider
paragraphs: Give each shortlisted provider the same approved business requirements and ask it to demonstrate four situations: a routine estimate request, an existing customer changing a booking, a request outside the service area and a transfer recipient who is unavailable. These are proposed evaluation scenarios, not tests Revo has conducted on the listed providers.

Record the information captured, the system where it appeared and the next step assigned to your team. Keep service acceptance, diagnosis, estimates and dispatch under your business’s rules. Use the existing selection and booking guides to prepare those requirements; this comparison contributes provider-specific documentation rather than replacing that planning work.
items: Ask where the estimate request is stored.
Check the supported handling of an appointment change.
Review the response to an out-of-area request.
Check the unavailable-recipient fallback and follow-up owner.

faqs.q: Do all AI receptionists connect to the same field-service software?
faqs.a: No. Compare the named integration and its documented operations. Verify the exact plan, software account and booking actions with the provider; a general calendar or integration claim is not evidence of every field-service workflow.

faqs.q: Does human handoff mean a receptionist supplied by the vendor?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A transfer to your team and access to a provider’s live receptionist are different arrangements. Confirm who answers, the fallback and any human-involvement charges.

faqs.q: Which alternative is best for my company?
faqs.a: The documentation supports a shortlist, not a universal winner. Choose against your required booking destination, coverage, handoff and written billing terms, then request a demonstration of your actual requirements.

takeaway: Choose the plan that supports your actual call workflow.

title: Business voicemail greetings for home service companies
description: Adapt four business voicemail greetings for open hours, after hours, planned closures and unanswered transfers, with recording and callback checks.
lead: Give callers clear words to hear before they leave a message.
intro: A business voicemail greeting should tell callers where they have arrived, what information to leave and what happens after the recording. For a home service company, a useful message asks for a callback number and a short description without implying that a job has been accepted.

sections.title: Before choosing a template
paragraphs: These four original sample recordings are starting points, not customer recordings or measured results. Replace every bracketed field, remove unsupported options and have the mailbox owner approve the callback wording before recording.

Write down the name callers should hear, the hours when messages are reviewed, the approved callback expectation and the mailbox owner. Choose a greeting that matches the route callers actually take. A busy-day recording, a closed-office recording and a planned-closure recording should not give contradictory information.

Ask only for the details needed to start follow-up. A name, callback number, service area or ZIP code, and brief request are usually enough for this sample workflow. Do not ask callers to record payment information, passwords, access codes or other sensitive details.

sections.title: 1. During business hours, when the team cannot answer
paragraphs: Original template: “You have reached the [Business name] service team. We are unable to answer this call. After the tone, tell us your name, callback number, service ZIP code and the work you are calling about. Our team reviews messages [review hours] and returns calls [approved callback expectation].”
items: Use when: the business is open but the call reaches a monitored mailbox.
Customize: use the real review schedule; do not substitute “right away” or a made-up response target. If the greeting becomes too long, omit the ZIP-code request and collect it on the callback.

sections.title: 2. After hours, when the office is closed
paragraphs: Original template: “This is [Business name]. Our office is closed, and our next message-review period begins [day and time, with time zone if needed]. Record your name, the number where we can reach you and a brief service request after the tone. Our callback expectation is [approved wording].”
items: Use when: callers reach a mailbox outside office hours.

Customize: a message-review time is not a technician arrival time. If the business does not monitor voicemail overnight, the recording must not suggest that it does. Do not add an on-call number, menu key or emergency-response promise unless that separate route really exists and has been verified.

sections.title: 3. A planned closure or holiday
paragraphs: Original template: “You have reached [Business name]. Our office is closed until [reopening date and time]. You can leave your name, callback number and a short description of your request after the tone. We will review messages [actual review period]. For current office hours, visit [short verified website address].”
items: Use when: the normal weekly schedule is temporarily different.

Customize: use the full reopening date, not “tomorrow.” Remove the website sentence if the linked page is not maintained. Set an internal reminder to restore the normal recording when the closure ends.

sections.title: 4. A transfer ends at a voicemail mailbox
paragraphs: Original template: “This is the [team or person's name] mailbox at [Business name]. The connection could not be completed. Leave your name, callback number and the reason you need this team after the tone. Messages are reviewed [actual review period], with callbacks [approved expectation].”
items: Use when: testing confirms that an unanswered transfer reaches this specific mailbox and accepts a recording.

Customize: do not say the recipient has already read a summary or accepted the request. If the call instead returns to an answering agent, use the existing live transfer-language guide rather than this recorded greeting.

sections.title: Check the recording and the mailbox
paragraphs: Read the script aloud at a natural pace in a quiet place. Keep only information the caller needs before leaving a message. Record and replay it to check the business name, numbers and dates are understandable. Avoid treating a particular duration as a universal rule.
Test from another phone under the actual routing conditions listed here.

For each test, confirm that the intended recording plays, the caller can leave a message, the message reaches the correct mailbox and its owner can retrieve it. These are proposed checks, not completed Revo tests. A recording alone does not establish message delivery or follow-up.

Phone-provider settings differ. Nextiva's documentation distinguishes a standard greeting from a busy greeting and describes mailbox notifications. RingCentral's documentation distinguishes a voicemail greeting from the greeting played when a caller first reaches an extension. Check the correct mailbox and route rather than assuming that changing one greeting changes them all.
items: An unanswered call during open hours.
A call outside the configured hours.
The temporary-closure route, if used.
An unavailable transfer recipient, if the setup supports that path.

faqs.q: Is a voicemail greeting the same as a phone answering script?
faqs.a: No. A voicemail greeting is recorded wording the caller hears before leaving a message. A live answering script supports a conversation and follow-up questions.

faqs.q: Should I promise a callback within a specific number of minutes?
faqs.a: Only use an expectation that the person responsible for callbacks has approved and can maintain. Publishing a time in a recording does not create staffing or availability.

faqs.q: Can I offer texting or a booking link in the recording?
faqs.a: Include only a route that is active, appropriate for the request and monitored. Do not assume the business number accepts texts or that a request form confirms an appointment.

faqs.q: Can Revo record or host these voicemail greetings?
faqs.a: This page does not establish that capability. The examples can be adapted for a voicemail system the business already uses. Confirm any proposed Revo call flow and supported features directly before changing routing.

takeaway: Match the recording to the mailbox and the callback plan.

title: ServiceTitan answering services: native AI and integrations
description: Review ServiceTitan's native Voice Agent and documented third-party answering options, with checks for booking, capacity and call reporting.
lead: Check what happens to the caller and the ServiceTitan record.
intro: Published by Revo. Documentation reviewed October 15, 2026. This guide describes published product capabilities, not independently tested performance. A Revo–ServiceTitan integration was not verified for this guide.

sections.title: Start with the ServiceTitan workflow you need
paragraphs: An answering service for a ServiceTitan business should be evaluated at two levels: what happens to the caller, and what appears in ServiceTitan afterward. A message sent to the office, a new job created in the platform and a correctly classified phone call are different results.

Start with the native option as well as external services. ServiceTitan has its own AI Voice Agent. Third-party providers also document connections, but a familiar software logo does not tell you which records a particular package can read or create. The examples below are documented options, not an exhaustive ranking.

sections.title: ServiceTitan's native AI Voice Agent
paragraphs: ServiceTitan's current Basic Phones and Phones Pro FAQ documents new-job booking, appointment changes, configured human escalation and call-outcome records. Its stated audience and package conditions are specific; ask ServiceTitan to confirm eligibility for your account and phone product. Do not assume the feature is included in every subscription.

Check the applicable capacity requirements, because the published documents describe different contexts. The Basic Phones and Phones Pro FAQ calls Adaptive Capacity configuration optional but highly recommended; the ServiceTitan Max pre-go-live checklist marks it required before enabling Voice Agent job booking. Confirm the applicable rollout with ServiceTitan rather than treating either statement as universal.

ServiceTitan's capacity documentation explains how availability depends on configured job durations, technician shifts, skills, zones and business units. Review those inputs with the person who owns scheduling; an answering agent is not a substitute for accurate operating rules.

sources.label: ServiceTitan Basic Phones / Phones Pro FAQ

sections.title: Avoca: documented API booking and capacity access
paragraphs: Avoca's entry in the ServiceTitan Marketplace is marked Certified Application. Its integration FAQ describes API access to AdCap data and booking jobs back into ServiceTitan. That is more specific than a generic promise to send call notes. Ask Avoca to show which actions are enabled for your account, how existing customers are matched and what happens when the requested booking is unavailable. Marketplace status does not by itself prove every possible workflow or a measured performance result.

sections.title: Dexcomm: live and AI answering with a documented connection
paragraphs: Dexcomm's integration page says its live and AI agents use an API connection to access customer and job information and book jobs in ServiceTitan. It describes either escalating to the business's team or leaving work for later handling according to the agreed on-call process. Confirm the chosen service arrangement, permitted actions and escalation rules in the actual proposal. Those published capabilities do not establish that every caller qualifies for a job or that every request receives immediate field service.

sections.title: Check the record, not just the answered call
paragraphs: ServiceTitan documents a case where a third-party answering service handles the caller but the call still appears abandoned. Its July help article describes profile-based call claiming or later reclassification for that workflow. Do not apply that article as a universal setup instruction.

Contact Center Pro has different handling: its current FAQ says agents cannot interact with core ServiceTitan call bubbles and describes reviewing the Call Journey in Conversation History. Identify whether the business uses Basic Phones, Phones Pro or Contact Center Pro before asking a provider how answered calls, booked jobs and unbooked requests will be recorded. Resolve an unclear classification workflow with ServiceTitan and the provider.

Routing can also affect visibility. The native Voice Agent FAQ warns that its forwarding number is not intended to be advertised directly to customers because direct calls are not logged in Search. Confirm the supported path from the public business number rather than treating any reachable number as an equivalent integration.

sources.label: ServiceTitan Basic Phones / Phones Pro FAQ

sections.title: Request a demonstration of these outcomes
paragraphs: Use authorized test data and ask the provider to demonstrate:
These are proposed acceptance checks, not tests performed by Revo on the listed providers. Inspect the actual account result and confirm the written service scope before routing customer traffic.
items: An existing customer requests a new job. Identify the customer/location record used and the job record created. Check for an unintended duplicate.
The requested slot is unavailable. Show the offered next step and who decides whether another time or manual review is appropriate.
A caller asks to change an appointment. Establish whether the chosen product and configuration can make that change or must hand it to staff.
No job is booked. Show the call record, classification and follow-up owner in the phone product the business actually uses.
The connection or human recipient is unavailable. Show the pending request, error visibility and recovery process rather than assuming the caller's message reached the right person.

faqs.q: Does ServiceTitan offer its own answering option?
faqs.a: Yes. Its documentation describes a native AI Voice Agent. Availability, configuration and account requirements should be confirmed for the specific phone product.

faqs.q: Does a forwarded call prove there is a ServiceTitan integration?
faqs.a: No. Forwarding proves a call reaches a destination. Ask separately what customer or job records are accessed or created and how the call is classified.

faqs.q: Does Revo have a verified ServiceTitan integration?
faqs.a: This guide did not verify a named connection. Revo's published plans describe field-service connections in general. Confirm the exact supported software, actions and plan directly; do not infer ServiceTitan compatibility from that category.

takeaway: Verify the workflow in the phone product you actually use.
